prior_art_threats: Some BBRv2/Cubic coexistence papers exist, but specific shallow-buffer edge switch focus with BBRv3 is rare.
Concept drift in standard ML is known, but silent recall collapse of fixed PQ codebooks without retraining is poorly documented.
Fuzzing memory allocators usually looks for safety bugs, not deterministic pathological fragmentation/OOM.
Adversarial ETA is studied, but testing extreme brittleness to trivial MTU/padding jitter on CICIDS2017 models is a highly specific empirical gap.
Serverless DB latency is known to be higher, but specific thundering-herd micro-burst page-cache invalidation curves are under-evaluated.
Popularity bias is known, but the specific interaction of Two-Tower initialization heuristics during high-velocity cold-start flooding is a distinct empirical measure.
Continual FL exists, but bimodal periodic flipping (oscillation without convergence) is rarely tested compared to static label skew.
Both ZeRO and Async checkpointing are studied individually; their overlapping PCIe bandwidth contention starvation is an untested hardware/software intersection.
Disparate impact of DP-SGD is somewhat known, but isolating the gradient clipping effect on *extreme* minority classes (<0.1%) recall collapse is highly specific.
While ALEX memory blowup under adversarial loads is studied, continuous boundary sequential inserts causing P99 latency spikes is a distinct measurement.
PTS is studied generally; evaluating FNR specifically partitioned by Refactoring vs Feature commits is a novel empirical benchmark.
CXL performance is active, but specific random-access graph workload penalty due to lack of prefetching on CXL is a strong architectural evaluation.
